text: "Rattlestar Ricklactica" is the fifth episode of the fourth season and the 36th episode overall of the Adult Swim animated series Rick and Morty. Written by James Siciliano and directed by Jacob Hair, it originally aired on December 15, 2019. While setting up Christmas lights, Jerry falls off the roof and is zapped by Rick with a ray that renders him lighter than air for 10 hours, then makes his shoes heavier than air, resulting in neutral buoyancy and allowing him to jump higher than usual. Rick and Morty leave for an adventure, but their ship breaks down in space; while repairing it, Morty is bitten by a snake astronaut and kills it. To atone for the snake's death, Morty buys another snake from a pet store and sends her to a race-war-ridden snake planet, where the snakes quickly realize she is from a different world. This leads to an increasing number of snakes that alternately attack or protect the Smiths. Rick explains that Morty's actions caused the snakes to unite and invent time travel. Rick and Morty travel to the Snake Pentagon to end the war, but the snakes' time machine is incomplete. A future version of Rick and Morty, who has a black eye, appears with a snake-language book containing time travel instructions and insults their past selves. Current Rick and Morty travel to 1985 and leave the book at Snake MIT. Meanwhile, Jerry loses one of his shoes, causing him to float away helplessly. Believing he will either survive unassisted or be blamed by Rick and Beth if he dies, he refuses help. With minutes left on the ray and high above the ground, Jerry prepares to fall when a jet passes by, which he attaches himself to. The plane crashes after colliding with a flying snake, but Jerry survives. Back on present-day Earth, the large amount of time travel alerts the Time Cops from "A Rickle in Time," who travel back in time and kill the first primitive snake to use tools, preventing snake civilization and causing the snakes to vanish. Jerry reveals he has been on the roof the entire time, turns on the Christmas lights, then falls off and breaks his leg, which Rick heals to 50% capacity, leaving the rest of the healing to Jerry. Rick and Morty are reminded by their future selves to make the time travel notes. In the post-credits scene, while waiting for their past selves on the snake planet, Rick tells Morty to stay in the car next time and punches him in the eye. Rick and Morty's journey to Snake MIT is set to a chalkboard displaying mathematics related to quantum mechanics, known as the snake equation. The notation on the board was inspired by a research paper by Christopher Wood, Jacob Biamonte, and David G. Cory published in the journal Quantum Information & Computation and later included in a book by Jacob Biamonte. The episode aired on Adult Swim on December 15, 2019. According to Nielsen Media Research, it was viewed by 1.32 million household viewers in the United States and achieved a 0.75 rating among the 18–49 adult demographic, making it the lowest-rated episode of the series (excluding the unannounced season three premiere) since season one's "M. Night Shaym-Aliens!". Zack Handlen of The A.V. Club awarded the episode an A, calling it the best episode of the season so far and a pure joy from start to finish, noting it is funny despite not being revolutionary or emotionally impactful, and restoring faith in the show. Joe Matar of Den of Geek gave it a 5 out of 5, stating that the first half of Rick and Morty's fourth season ends strongly with this not-so-festive Christmas episode.
